title: Let’s Talk About AI
text:
The CESAB Experience

Autonomy to assess which algorithms fit your research question (ai-ecol.github.io) \(\rightarrow\) Translated into 4 Core Insights (Today’s Roadmap)




Insight 1 · AI > Generative Chatbots Section 1: Distinguish GenAI from the wider AI taxonomy (ML, DL, Symbolic AI).


Insight 2 · Domain Baseline Primes Section 2: Your (e.g. ecological) knowledge anchors plausibility and dictates how a problem is framed.




Insight 3 · Exhaust Traditional Methods Section 2: Verify dimensionality and exhaust classical statistical analyses as a first step.


Insight 4 · Explicit Trade-Offs Section 3: Balance predictive gain against explainability based on the scientific goal.





Note: This session is a synthesis of CESAB Day 1 principles — not a full 5-day syllabus dump. Session 2 (10:45 a.m.) shows how these insights landed in my PhD.

title: Let’s Talk About AI
section: Why Learn AI? A Bio-Inspired Paradox
text:
Why Learn AI? A Bio-Inspired Paradox
As a scientist trained to look for mechanistic explanations, why invest in learning “black-box” algorithms?



Biological Signal Integration (Human Learning)

Biological neurons integrate electrochemical inputs across complex networks.
Scientific understanding emerges through effortful cognitive friction—writing, debugging, synthesizing, and testing hypotheses.


[IMAGE: Biological Neuron / Synaptic Integration] Save file as: assets/images/bio_neuron.png 





Artificial Neuron (Perceptron, 1957)

Loosely inspired by biology: Inputs \(\rightarrow\) Weights \(\rightarrow\) Weighted Sum \(\rightarrow\) Activation \(\rightarrow\) Output.
Parameter estimation is numerical loss minimization—not biological reasoning or comprehension.


[IMAGE: Perceptron Diagram (CESAB Day 1 Slide 70)] Save file as: assets/images/artificial_perceptron.png 





The Paradox: AI delivers major scientific breakthroughs (e.g., AlphaFold), yet our most frequent daily contact is with Generative AI chatbots. When misused to bypass writing, literature synthesis, or coding, a bio-inspired tool short-circuits our own biological learning process.

title: Let’s Talk About AI
text:
Epistemic & Ecological Guardrails (Insight 1a)




Cognitive Proletarianization: Externalizing analytical tasks erodes our savoir-faire and methodological metacognition (Stiegler, 2010).
Empirical Evidence on Cognition: Controlled studies indicate that over-reliance on GenAI can reduce knowledge retention (Barcaui, 2025), lower persistence and independent performance (Liu et al., 2026, preprint), and foster dependence/deskilling (Kim et al., 2025).
Illusions of Understanding: Fluent outputs can mask weak epistemic grounding (Messeri & Crockett, 2024)—sparking active debate across French doctoral schools on protecting core research training.
Pragmatic Guardrail: Retain cognitive friction for reasoning, writing, and analysis. Delegate routine formatting or syntax checks; shift from “Do X” to “Critique / explain X”.





Material & Ecological Footprint

Global energy-economy modeling shows AI productivity gains can drive net \(\text{CO}_2\) increases via rebound effects (Alpine et al., 2026).
Infrastructure expansion concentrates in water-stressed regions (e.g., Uruguay: 1.77 and Chile: 3.49 data centers per 1M inhabitants; IFC, 2026).


[IMAGE: IFC 2026 Data Centers Map — Uruguay 1.77] Save file as: assets/images/datacenters_uruguay_ifc2026.png 


“Only a tiny proportion of water in Uruguay is used for human consumption.” — Daniel Pena (Rest of World, 2026)





Stiegler (2010) For a New Critique of Political Economy · Messeri & Crockett (2024) Nature 10.1038/s41586-024-07146-0 · Barcaui (2025) SSH Open 10.1016/j.ssaho.2025.102287 · Kim et al. (2025) Consum. Psychol. Rev. 10.1002/arcp.70008 · Liu et al. (2026) arXiv:2604.04721 · Alpine et al. (2026) npj Clim. Action 10.1038/s44168-026-00411-0

title: Let’s Talk About AI
text:
Navigating the AI Vocabulary
In practice, researchers encounter a scattered soup of overlapping terms and tools:


Linear & Logistic Regression ChatGPT / Claude / Perplexity Symbolic Logic & Rules PCA / UMAP CNN & RNN Data Science & Statistics Random Forest & Decision Trees Intelligent Robots Neural Networks (MLP) Support Vector Machines (SVM) Knowledge Representation


Which field contains which—and where do everyday chatbots actually sit?

title: Let’s Talk About AI
text:
Navigating the AI Vocabulary
Organizing the umbrella into parallel domains and nested subsets:

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (Umbrella Discipline)



Symbolic AI, Reasoning & Embodied Systems

Symbolic Logic & Rules Knowledge Representation Intelligent Robots


Explicit rules, ontologies, and constraint solving (e.g., protected-area design in CESAB Day 5).


Overlapping Quantitative Pillar Data Science & Statistics





MACHINE LEARNING (Automated Learning from Data)

Linear & Logistic Regression PCA / UMAP Support Vector Machines (SVM) Random Forest & Decision Trees


DEEP LEARNING (Multi-Layer Neural Networks)

Neural Networks (MLP) CNN & RNN


GENERATIVE AI & LLMs (A small, highly visible subset) ChatGPT / Claude / Perplexity







Standard reference taxonomy: The OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems classifies systems by model type (symbolic, statistical, or hybrid), learning paradigm, and transparency.


Optional backup: You can keep assets/images/oecd_ai_classification.png in your backup folder or click the live OECD link during Q&A if anyone asks for formal regulatory criteria.

title: Let’s Talk About AI
section: When Does a Research Problem Need ML?
text:
When Does a Research Problem Need ML?
Scenario: An environmental scientist monitors 100 river sites across chemical concentrations, water quality, climate, and community traits.



What Is a “Dimension”?

In Ecology / Env. Science: Usually 3D physical space \((x, y, z)\) + time.
In Machine Learning: Every measured variable is an axis (\(d\)). Measuring 50 water chemistry & species variables places each site in a 50-dimensional space.



The Curse of High Dimensionality
In a unit hypercube with \(n=100\) samples, the edge length \(l = (k/n)^{1/d}\) needed to capture even \(k=1\) neighbor grows rapidly:



Dimensions (\(d\))
2
3
10
100




Cube edge (\(l\))
0.10
0.21
0.63
0.955



Distance flattens; almost every observation lies near the “border.”




[IMAGE: CESAB Day 1 — Hypercube Distance & 3D-to-2D Manifold] Save file as: assets/images/curse_dim_cube_manifold.png 


The Methodological Filter

Low \(d\), linear/known structure? Traditional statistics are sufficient and preferable.
High \(d\), sparse space? Dimensionality reduction (PCA, UMAP) and ML help uncover lower intrinsic dimensionality (manifolds).

title: Let’s Talk About AI
section: Demystifying ML: Scaling One Research Question
text:
Demystifying ML: Scaling One Research Question
Following the same environmental dataset from classical statistics into the ML toolkit:



1. Classical Baseline One predictor, linear trend: \(Y = ax + b + \varepsilon\)
Solved analytically via Ordinary Least Squares.




→




2. Same Problem as ML Any ML workflow = 3 parts:

Model (equation)
Loss function (error metric, e.g., MSE)
Solver (iterative step, e.g., gradient descent)





→




3. Earned Complexity Add non-linear thresholds, categories, or high-\(d\) features:
Move deliberately along the toolkit \(\rightarrow\) Classification (Cross-Entropy), Random Forests, SVMs, or Neural Nets.








Classical Statistics Dictionary


Machine Learning Dictionary


Scientific Note




Covariates / Explanatory variables (\(X\))


Features / Inputs


Domain knowledge guides selection




Response variable (\(Y\)) & Residuals


Target / Label & Loss Function


Defines what is optimized




Mechanistic / Biological parameters


Weights / Hyperparameters


Often have no biological meaning






Check before scaling up: Exhaust classical exploratory data analysis first. Complex algorithms are justified only when data shape and dimensionality demand them.

text:
Interactive Checkpoint: Frame Your Question



How would you formulate one question from your own research as \(Y \sim X\)?


In Slido 3 (Code: #3791 5273), write a short 1-line formulation:

Target (\(Y\)): What do you want to explain or predict? (continuous value or category?)
Features (\(X\)): What predictors do you have—and roughly how many dimensions (\(d\))?
Priority: Do you care more about mechanistic inference or predictive accuracy?

title: Let’s Talk About AI
section: The Two Cultures & The Flexible Trade-Off
text:
The Two Cultures & The Flexible Trade-Off



Data Modeling Culture (Classical Statistics)

Assumes data arise from a specified stochastic/mechanistic process (e.g., GLMMs, ODEs).
Primary goal: Parameter inference, uncertainty quantification, and causal interpretation.





↔︎




Algorithmic Modeling Culture (Machine Learning)

Treats the underlying data-generating mechanism as unknown or too complex to write analytically.
Primary goal: Out-of-sample predictive accuracy across high-dimensional, non-linear interactions.





High InterpretabilityLinear / Mechanistic (GUTS) ← Hybrid & Explainable AI (XAI) →Decision Trees · Random Forests + Feature Importance High Predictive CapacityDeep Neural Networks


A Pragmatic, Objective-Driven Choice: Interpretability is not a dogma—it is an explicit scientific decision. High-throughput screening (e.g., QSARs) may justify prioritizing accuracy; regulatory or mechanistic risk assessment demands explainability. Increasingly, hybrid pipelines combine both.


Breiman, L. (2001). Statistical modeling: The two cultures. Statistical Science, 16(3), 199–231. 10.1214/ss/1009213726 · Rudin, C. (2019). Stop explaining black box machine learning models for high stakes decisions and use interpretable models instead. Nature Machine Intelligence, 1, 206–215. 10.1038/s42256-019-0048-x

text:
Closing the Loop & Bridge to Part 2



Revisit Slide 2: Our Opening Word Cloud

Where did our collective word cloud cluster 45 minutes ago?
AI is not synonymous with chatbots—it is an organized toolkit spanning symbolic logic, classical ML, deep learning, and generative models.


[LIVE CALLBACK: Switch to Slido 1 Word Cloud tab] (Post-event: final exported word cloud will be archived on the workshop website)





How These 4 Insights Reshaped My PhD (Preview of Part 2 — Today at 10:45)

Exhausted traditional statistics first (descriptive & linear multivariate audits) before invoking ML.
Kept mechanistic models (GUTS) at the core where biological interpretability is essential.
Deployed ML as an explainable meta-model to audit which experimental design features govern parameter precision.

title: Let’s Talk About AI
text:
Take-Home Messages




AI is an Umbrella Toolkit: Know the taxonomy before choosing an algorithm—GenAI chatbots are only one narrow subset.


Protect Cognitive Friction: Preserve your scientific savoir-faire and remain aware of the ecological footprint of GenAI workflows.


Earn Model Complexity: Check true dimensionality and exhaust classical statistical analyses before adopting ML.


Align the Trade-Off to Your Goal: Use domain knowledge to decide where interpretability is essential, where predictive power wins, or where hybrid approaches bridge both.
